1:
Let $t$ be hours after midnight. Minimum 2000 ft at $t=3$, maximum 2500 ft at $t=7.5$: half-period $4.5$ h, period $9$ h, midline $2250$, amplitude $250$. Starting from the minimum:
\[A(t)=2250-250\cos\!\Big(\frac{2\pi}{9}(t-3)\Big).\]
$A<2100\iff\cos\!\big(\frac{2\pi}{9}(t-3)\big)>0.6$. With $\alpha=\cos^{-1}(0.6)\approx0.9273$, this means $\frac{2\pi}{9}(t-3)\in(-\alpha+2\pi k,\ \alpha+2\pi k)$, i.e. $t\in(3-1.328+9k,\ 3+1.328+9k)$. On $[0,24]$:
\[(1.672,4.328),\ (10.672,13.328),\ (19.672,22.328),\]
each $2.656$ h long. Total: \boxed{\approx 7.97\ \text{hours}}.
2:
Let $t$ be years after 1980. Gumbolantenden: $G(t)=20000(1.0107)^t$.

Attalioto: $A(20)=40000$, $A(25)=62000$, so its yearly factor is $b=(62000/40000)^{1/5}=1.55^{1/5}\approx1.09161$ and
\[A(t)=40000\,b^{\,t-20}.\]
Set $G(t)=A(t)$ and take logs:
\[\ln20000+t\ln1.0107=\ln40000+(t-20)\ln b\ \Rightarrow\ t=\frac{20\ln b-\ln 2}{\ln b-\ln1.0107}\approx\boxed{13.76\ \text{years after 1980}}\]
(both about 23{,}160 people, in late 1993).
3:
\textbf{(a)} Nell covers $\langle1-20,\,4-8\rangle=\langle-19,-4\rangle$ in 3 s:
\[x(t)=20-\frac{19}{3}t,\qquad y(t)=8-\frac43t.\]
\textbf{(b)} Kit moves along $y=-0.5x+2.5$ toward the $y$-axis (decreasing $x$). Direction $\langle-1,\,0.5\rangle$, length $\sqrt{1.25}=\frac{\sqrt5}{2}$, so the unit direction is $\langle-\frac{2}{\sqrt5},\frac1{\sqrt5}\rangle$. At 5 ft/s from $(1,2)$:
\[x(t)=1-2\sqrt5\,t\approx1-4.472t,\qquad y(t)=2+\sqrt5\,t\approx2+2.236t.\]
4:
Put Albany at $(0,0)$ (East $=+x$, North $=+y$). Birmingham is $(7,10)$ and Cambridge is $(7+3,\,10-4)=(10,6)$.

Bob's position: $(7s,10s)$, $0\le s\le1$. Squared distance to Cambridge:
\[D(s)=(7s-10)^2+(10s-6)^2=149s^2-260s+136,\]
minimized at $s=\frac{260}{298}=\frac{130}{149}\approx0.8725$ (inside $[0,1]$), the point $(6.107,\,8.725)$. Closest distance:
\[\sqrt{(10-6.107)^2+(6-8.725)^2}\approx\boxed{4.75\ \text{km}}.\]
5:
Let $d$ be the first distance and $h$ Godzilla's height then. First: $h=d\tan73^\circ$. Second (120 ft farther, height $h+24$): $h+24=(d+120)\tan66^\circ$.

Substitute: $d\tan73^\circ+24=(d+120)\tan66^\circ$, so
\[d=\frac{120\tan66^\circ-24}{\tan73^\circ-\tan66^\circ}\approx239.58\ \text{ft},\qquad h\approx783.6\ \text{ft}.\]
At the second measurement Godzilla was $h+24\approx\boxed{807.6\ \text{ft}}$ tall.
6:
Let $s$ be the side of each square and $w$ the short side of the rectangle (long side $2w$). Fencing (each enclosure fenced separately):
\[3(4s)+2(w+2w)=12s+6w=300\ \Rightarrow\ w=50-2s,\quad 0\le s\le25.\]
Total area:
\[A(s)=3s^2+2w^2=3s^2+2(50-2s)^2=11s^2-400s+5000.\]
This parabola opens \emph{upward}, so its vertex $s=\frac{200}{11}\approx18.2$ ft gives the \emph{minimum} total area ($\approx1364$ ft$^2$). On $0\le s\le25$ the maximum is at an endpoint: $A(0)=5000$, $A(25)=1875$.

\textbf{Answer:} the total area is largest when the squares are as small as possible ($s\to0$, area approaching $5000$ ft$^2$, all fencing in the rectangle). If the question intends the vertex of the parabola, note that $s=\frac{200}{11}\approx18.18$ ft is where the area is smallest, not largest.

\textbf{(a)} For $x\ge1$: $|x-1|=x-1$, so $f(x)=2x+5-4x+4=-2x+9$. For $x<1$: $|x-1|=1-x$, so $f(x)=2x+5-4+4x=6x+1$.
\[f(x)=\begin{cases}6x+1, & x<1\\ -2x+9, & x\ge1\end{cases}\]
\textbf{(b)} If $a\ge1$: $-2a+9=7a-8\Rightarrow a=\frac{17}{9}$, which is $\ge1$ \checkmark. If $a<1$: $6a+1=7a-8\Rightarrow a=9$, not $<1$, rejected.
\[\boxed{a=\tfrac{17}{9}}\]
